comments.textRawHtml:
Back in highschool, simulating different elevator algorithms was one of the projects I implemented during my CS class. It wasn't for the class — AP CS did not require anything like actual programming — but it was a fun project.

A cool connection is that a spinning-disk hard drive (HDD) is actually kind of like one really long elevator, just wrapped around a spindle instead of perfectly vertical. The SCAN algorithm is actually a disk-scheduling algorithm!

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elevator_algorithm

一个很酷的联系是，旋转磁盘硬盘 (HDD) 实际上有点像一个很长的电梯，只是缠绕在主轴上，而不是完全垂直。 SCAN算法实际上是一种磁盘调度算法！

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elevator_algorithm

children.textRawHtml: It's fun that the same algorithm applies to two different problems. In the disk case, the only unpredictable thing is future requests. So it's doubly fun that the same algorithm works in both cases!

comments.author: omoikane
comments.textRawHtml:
> Destination Dispatch [...] are in general worse

I wonder if this is an artifact of how the author used random destinations. I worked in a building that used Destination Dispatch, and the common travel pattern seemed to be:

- Everyone who is not on the ground floor generally want to go to the ground floor.

- People who are on the ground floor generally travel in large groups to the same destination.

This happens because people who worked on the same floor often leave for lunch at the same time, and return at the same time to the same floor. Destination Dispatch helps in this case because it's batching large groups of people with the same destination.

- 不在底层的每个人通常都想去底层。

发生这种情况是因为在同一楼层工作的人经常在同一时间出发吃午饭，并在同一时间返回同一楼层。 目的地调度在这种情况下会有所帮助，因为它会将大量人员分批发送到同一目的地。

children.author: _kb
children.textRawHtml:
The data is already there. This also gets more interesting when you expand the scope from just elevators to general building occupancy and movement.

In the simplest sense, I've seen this tied into security gates so as people badge on when entering the building there's already suitable elevator movement to meet demand by time the foot traffic reaches the lift lobby. That can then also feed into destination dispatch if you move from just people counts to identity (and known/most likely work floor).

From there you can move into wifi trilateration and have a live and quite accurate view of both how and who interacts with a physical space. This can feed into HVAC load shedding, JIT bookings for meeting rooms or workspaces, and a lot of very good things from a sustainability and general optimisation perspective. The flip side is it also has the potential to be an absolute dystopian privacy nightmare.

children.author: TeMPOraL
children.textRawHtml:
> (...) and a lot of very good things from a sustainability and general optimisation perspective. The flip side is it also has the potential to be an absolute dystopian privacy nightmare.

Privacy is an illusion for most people, and in office spaces, it's also a red herring. Wifi trilateration doesn't make things worse when you have a CCTV camera on every corner, badge reader at every other door, and presence sensing in conference rooms. Dystopia does not materialize without a severe regime shift.

Nah, my main worry is precisely sustainability and optimization, i.e. cost-cutting, because the more tools you give a business to optimize, and the more bullshit excuses ("sustainability! saving the planet!") you give a business, the worse the outcome is for users (here: employees). And a lot of that is doubly annoying, because it's counter-productive.

So what you have smart sensors in every room, and combine it with badge readers and wifi trilat and what not, and have smart auto-routing/rebooking algorithm: half the week, all conference rooms are always booked full, and yet somehow when you physically go and check, a good half sits empty, and it's apparently an impossible problem to solve.

So what the bathroom wall says, "with water-saving fixtures, we're using much less water in this building", and "we're now saving 2L water per flush". It's all bullshit, because those eco inventions mean I need to flush 3 times instead of once, and it means that I spend a minute washing my hands instead of 10 seconds - especially because both the soap and the dispenser are also optimized, so it takes 20 seconds to get enough soap on your hands, and then extra 20 seconds to get it off afterwards, because unlike normal people soap, it leaves your hands slippery for some reason.

And then they say "scientists said you can dry your hands with just 2 paper towels". At that point I'm getting red, because yes, I saw that TED talk 15 years ago too, and yes, it's total bullshit. Maybe it was true then, but the industry and the beancounters have value-optimized paper towels 15 times since that.

The generalization and summary of this rant is: slack is good. Happiness lives in slack. There is such thing as optimizing too much. Also the small, isolated systems under optimization, are in reality neither small nor isolated.
children.textZhHtml:
> (...) 从可持续性和一般优化的角度来看，有很多非常好的东西。另一方面，它也有可能成为绝对的反乌托邦隐私噩梦。

隐私对大多数人来说是一种幻想，在办公空间中，它也是一种转移注意力的东西。当每个角落都有闭路电视摄像头、每扇门都有徽章阅读器以及会议室中存在感应功能时，Wifi 三边测量不会让事情变得更糟。如果没有严重的政权更迭，反乌托邦就不会实现。

不，我主要担心的是可持续性和优化，即削减成本，因为你为企业提供的优化工具越多，你为企业提供的废话借口（“可持续发展！拯救地球！”）越多，对用户（这里是员工）来说，结果就越糟糕。其中很多都是双重烦人的，因为它适得其反。

所以你在每个房间都有智能传感器，并将其与徽章阅读器和 WiFi Trilat 等相结合，并具有智能自动路由/重新预订算法：半周，所有会议室总是被订满，但不知何故，当你亲自去检查时，有很大一半是空的，这显然是一个不可能解决的问题。

所以浴室墙上说的是， “有了节水装置，我们在这栋建筑中的用水量大大减少了”，“我们现在每次冲水可节省 2 升水”。这都是废话，因为那些生态发明意味着我需要冲水 3 次而不是一次，这意味着我要花一分钟而不是 10 秒洗手 - 特别是因为肥皂和分配器也都经过优化，所以需要 20 秒才能将足够的肥皂弄到手上，然后需要额外的 20 秒才能将其取下，因为与普通人的肥皂不同，它会因某种原因让你的手变得湿滑。

然后他们说“科学家说你只需2张纸巾就能擦干双手”。那时我脸红了，因为是的，15 年前我也看过那个 TED 演讲，是的，这完全是胡说八道。也许当时确实如此，但自那以后，行业和会计人员已经将价值优化的纸巾进行了 15 次。

这段咆哮的概括和总结是：松弛是好事。幸福生活在悠闲中。存在优化过度之类的问题。而且，正在优化的小型孤立系统实际上既不小也不孤立。

children.author: ufmace
children.textRawHtml:
> The generalization and summary of this rant is: slack is good. Happiness lives in slack. There is such thing as optimizing too much. Also the small, isolated systems under optimization, are in reality neither small nor isolated.

Yeah there's a certain type of engineer mindset that loves the idea of optimizing things. But if you want to really optimize something, you have to carefully account for every single possible factor, situation, and use-case. Miss anything, and it's a much bigger disaster than saving 2% of whatever resource. It's rarely worth it.

Much better to treat the presumptions as a vague heuristic, make generous assumptions and add some slack, and call that good enough. Now there's probably enough slack to cover most of the edge cases you didn't think of, other things you based your original assumptions on changing under you, etc.
children.textZhHtml:
> 这个咆哮的概括和总结是：松弛是好的。幸福生活在悠闲中。存在优化过度之类的问题。此外，正在优化的小型、孤立的系统实际上既不小也不孤立。

是的，有某种类型的工程师思维方式喜欢优化事物的想法。但如果你想真正优化某些东西，你必须仔细考虑每一个可能的因素、情况和用例。错过任何事情都会比节省 2% 的资源带来更大的灾难。这是不值得的。

最好将这些假设视为模糊的启发式方法，做出慷慨的假设并增加一些宽松度，并称其足够好。现在可能有足够的余量来涵盖您没有想到的大多数边缘情况，您基于最初假设的其他事情等。

children.author: ent001
children.textRawHtml:
This is my biggest problem with the current state of things. The loss in quality of life out weights the gains in productivity. And they are concentrated on highly conscientiousness individuals, those who already got silently taxed with most of the 80% of the work to get the last 20% of the results. So it is now compounding, if you care your workload will approximate 99,99..% of the total workload divided by the number of high conscientiousness individuals in your team/organization.

The current hype cycle might even represent a net global gain like some people argue. But it represents yet more externality driven exploitation. Remains to be seen what the new equilibrium will be given that now the population being exploited is not only close to the core of the world system but also already overburdened.

I do think it represents a mere acceleration of the previous trend that resulted since around 2005 in an explosion of average (not median) pay for software developers due to similar dynamics. If the system settles on a new level of pay that manages to convince enough people of enough skill to go along, it might just hum along and not implode. As for the rest of us, welcome to the growing permanent underclass and brace for the impact of the climate wars. We will be the fodder that will insulate the chosen ones under their air conditioned domes.
children.textZhHtml:

comments.author: hn_submit
comments.textRawHtml:
To me this merely signals how broken C++ development really is. Most if not all of the bugs being uncovered are memory related and therefore intimately tied to the mental memory model of C and C++, namely manual memory management.

It's fine for a C or C++ program encompassing a couple hundred lines but beyond that it's a liability.

C and C++ are simply not fit for purpose when large scale software projects are concerned. All of these need to be ported to Rust or another memory-safe language ASAP to prevent mayhem.

The hundreds if not thousands of developers working on Chrome weren't idiots who didn't know what they're doing. The complexity of programming in C/C++ is simply beyond most intelligent individuals' ability to get perfect all the time.

对于包含几百行的 C 或 C++ 程序来说没问题，但超出范围就成了负担。

当涉及大型软件项目时，C 和 C++ 根本不适合使用。所有这些都需要尽快移植到 Rust 或其他内存安全语言，以防止混乱。

数百甚至数千名使用 Chrome 的开发人员并不是白痴，他们不知道自己在做什么。 C/C++ 编程的复杂性根本超出了大多数聪明人始终完美的能力。

children.author: gtowey
children.textRawHtml:
I'll await your Rust ports of Windows, Linux and MacOS then.

This isn't really a fair take. Keep in mind that C/C++ has been the backbone of the most important software in the world since the 1970s. At that time we didn't have virtually unlimited compute and memory at our fingertips the way we do now. It was a huge improvement to have a high level language which still could be optimized nearly as well as assembly.

Its staying power is due to the fact that we really haven't had many good alternatives until maybe the last few years. Things are not going to get ported and rewritten overnight, especially when they largely just work like Linux & PostgreSQL. We'd nuke a huge amount of institutional knowledge and inertia to change those up.

And C/C++ are still key in the embedded space where we still have devices constrained on compute and memory. That's not going to go away anytime soon.

This criticism feel like someone complaining about why anyone still uses horses on the day the Model T was announced. Change takes time.
children.textZhHtml:
那么我将等待您的 Windows、Linux 和 MacOS 的 Rust 移植。

这确实不公平。请记住，自 20 世纪 70 年代以来，C/C++ 一直是世界上最重要软件的支柱。 当时我们并没有像现在那样拥有几乎无限的计算和内存。拥有一种高级语言是一个巨大的进步，它仍然可以像汇编一样进行优化。

它的持久力是因为我们直到最近几年才真正有很多好的替代方案。事情不会在一夜之间被移植和重写，尤其是当它们基本上像 Linux 和 PostgreSQL 一样工作时。我们会消除大量的机构知识和惯性来改变这些。

C/C++ 仍然是嵌入式领域的关键，在嵌入式领域，我们的设备仍然受到计算和内存的限制。这种情况不会很快消失。

这种批评感觉就像有人在抱怨为什么有人在 T 型车发布的那天仍然使用马。改变需要时间。

children.author: tikhonj
children.textRawHtml:
A pretty big part of the reason we didn't switch earlier is that most people—certainly most non-technical leaders, but also a lot of engineers—don't value correctness or security enough. We didn't have good alternatives until recently because we did not, collectively, invest in developing these alternatives.

One surprising thing is that, in the grand scheme of things, developing an alternative like Rust is not that expensive. It takes something like a small team a few years. Maybe a person-decade of effort to get to a viable point? Maybe two, whatever. The industry as a whole throws away orders of magnitude more engineering-years than that on vanity projects and internal dysfunction every year.

Of course, even once we have an alternative, the switching costs are high. And the barriers are far more social, organizational and political than they are technical. But even so, moving to alternatives incrementally has been viable for decades. And hey, if we include moves to garbage collected languages, we have been moving quite a bit... but we could have been moving more. It was only a matter of will and, upstream of that, cultural change.

So really, the problem isn't that people complain too much, it's that they don't complain enough :)
children.textZhHtml:
我们没有更早进行切换的很大一部分原因是大多数人（当然是大多数非技术领导者，但也包括很多工程师）对正确性或安全性的重视程度不够。直到最近我们才找到好的替代方案，因为我们没有集体投资开发这些替代方案。

令人惊讶的是，从宏观角度来看，开发像 Rust 这样的替代方案并不那么昂贵。一个小团队需要几年的时间。也许需要一个人十年的努力才能达到可行的程度？也许是两个，无论如何。整个行业每年丢弃的工程年数比虚荣项目和内部功能障碍的工程年数要多几个数量级。

当然，即使我们有替代方案，转换成本也很高。这些障碍更多地是社会、组织和政治方面的，而不是技术方面的。但即便如此，几十年来，逐步转向替代品仍然是可行的。嘿，如果我们包括对垃圾收集语言的移动，我们已经移动了很多......但我们本来可以移动更多。这只是一个意愿问题，而更重要的是文化变革。

Pre-Rust "serious C++ folks" used it because it was the best option if you wanted essentially zero performance overhead no heavy runtime and GC spikes. They didn't like the lack of memory safety but it was seen as an unfortunate but necessary trade-off.

children.author: gtowey
children.textRawHtml:
> And the barriers are far more social, organizational and political than they are technical.

At the core it's even more of an economic barrier which isn't even unique to capitalism.

I recall an article talking about why the Romans didn't invent steam engines and things like railroads considering people were aware that steam could be used to do work. The answer was largely that slave labor was so cheap that nobody really cared about finding more efficiency. It didn't solve any problem they had at the time.

The analogy transfers to the tech industry today, economics tend to drive most decisions. While I love technology and think research and innovation is important for its own sake -- particularly because we might not know what we're missing out on unless we explore -- but those controlling the purse strings have other priorities.

Others might point out that the economic cost of the bugs and failure cases in programming languages without memory safety might actually be greater than the cost of developing alternatives or accepting less performance in exchange for correctness. They're probably right! But unless you can measure it and present it on a spreadsheet to the management class, they won't acknowledge or understand it. It's really difficult to measure "incidents you didn't have". In any case it still might be cheaper to work on the next big startup idea, hype it & sell equity -- that strategy has produced trillion-dollar valuations recently. However correctly or incorrectly that may be, the benefit to an elite few is very real.
children.textZhHtml:
> 这些障碍更多地是社会性、组织性和政治性的，而不是技术性的。

从本质上讲，它更多的是一种经济障碍，这甚至不是资本主义所独有的。

我记得一篇文章讨论了为什么罗马人没有发明蒸汽机和铁路之类的东西，因为人们意识到蒸汽可以用来做功。 答案主要是奴隶劳动力是如此便宜，以至于没有人真正关心如何提高效率。 它没有解决他们当时遇到的任何问题。

这个类比转移到今天的科技行业，经济往往会驱动大多数决策。 虽然我热爱技术，并且认为研究和创新本身就很重要——特别是因为除非我们探索，否则我们可能不知道我们会错过什么——但那些控制钱包的人有其他优先事项。

其他人可能会指出，没有内存安全的编程语言中的错误和失败案例的经济成本实际上可能大于开发替代方案或接受较低性能以换取正确性的成本。 他们可能是对的！但除非你可以衡量它并将其以电子表格形式呈现给管理阶层，否则他们不会承认或理解它。衡量“你没有发生过的事件”确实很困难。无论如何，研究下一个大型创业想法、对其进行炒作并出售股权可能仍然更便宜——该策略最近产生了数万亿美元的估值。无论正确或错误，少数精英的利益是非常真实的。

DS Flash is where local models begin to feel useful for coding, but the quants we run locally are sharply reduced in intelligence from the benchmarks for the full models.

For applications where data cannot leave the local network it’s good to have them. For actual coding work I can’t actually justify the power of electricity and cooling, let alone the expensive hardware, compared to hosted APIs.

children.author: doginasuit
children.textRawHtml:
To help explain AI to my elderly mother, I said it is like an alien intelligence on a planet too far away to directly observe Earth, and everything it knows about humanity and our world it learned from reading just about every book and website. You can ask it a question or to do some work and it can often give a useful response but it can never directly judge its accuracy if it relates to the physical world, it has only your judgment to work with.

Given that limitation, it is incredible what it can still accomplish. And when it falls short, it is often in a charming way, if you are open to seeing it that way. It reflects something like a child's understanding of the world, not entirely wrong, just incomplete.

The fluttering cubes that might have been bees or butterflies were my favorite part.
children.textZhHtml:
为了帮助向我年迈的母亲解释人工智能，我说它就像一个距离太远而无法直接观察地球的行星上的外星智能体，它通过阅读几乎每一本书和网站了解到有关人类和我们世界的一切。你可以问它一个问题或做一些工作，它通常可以给出有用的响应，但如果它与物理世界相关，它永远无法直接判断其准确性，它只能根据你的判断进行工作。

考虑到这一限制，它仍然可以完成令人难以置信的事情。当它达不到要求时，它通常会以一种迷人的方式出现，如果你愿意以这种方式看待它的话。它反映了孩子对世界的理解，并非完全错误，只是不完整。

那些可能是蜜蜂或蝴蝶的飘动的立方体是我最喜欢的部分。

children.author: Valakas_
children.textRawHtml:
That's a nice metaphor for your mother, i like it. I would just touch on one small part, which is that it has more than our judgement though. It has access to laws of physics, to formulas, to all our current scientific knowledge which we have shown to be correct by interacting with the physical world. It can create an (incomplete) model of the world based on verified theories already. Through deduction and reasoning alone it can get pretty far. After all, there's many scientific theories we created long in advance before we actually proved them to be correct through interaction with the physical world. So even before they were proved to be correct, they were already correct. Same can be applied to what LLM can infer through reasoning alone.

Anyway, just a small point which probably still wouldn't change the nice metaphor your made.
children.textZhHtml:
这是对你母亲的一个很好的比喻，我喜欢它。我只想谈一小部分，那就是它的内容超出了我们的判断。它可以获取物理定律、公式以及我们当前所有的科学知识，这些知识通过与物理世界的互动而被证明是正确的。它可以根据已验证的理论创建一个（不完整的）世界模型。仅通过演绎和推理就可以走得很远。毕竟，我们在通过与物理世界的相互作用实际证明它们是正确的之前就已经提前创建了许多科学理论。因此，即使在它们被证明是正确的之前，它们就已经是正确的了。同样的情况也适用于法学硕士仅通过推理就能推断出的内容。

无论如何，这只是一个小点，可能仍然不会改变你所做的漂亮比喻。

comments.author: NitpickLawyer
comments.textRawHtml:
This is more exciting than k3, IMO. Dsv4 models are extremely cheap to serve. Improving their capabilities has lots of downstream effects, as it becomes "good enough" for more and more tasks.

DS was serving the pro version at extremely low prices for a long time, and they've had integrations with opencode & other providers, so they likely gathered a lot of data from real developers doing real tasks (on openrouter they were labeled as such). Now they can use those live scenarios to further post-train their models and improve them further.

Can't wait to see if distilling k3 into dsv4 brings additional improvements. Anyway, having fast cheap models getting better is great for the community. Especially since these don't "go away" on a provider's whim. Whatever capabilities they get, can be used "forever" going forward. And, at least flash can be ran "at home" with <10k in hardware, which isn't really possible / feasible with glm/k3 larger models.

DS 长期以来以极低的价格提供专业版本，并且他们已经与 opencode 和其他提供商集成，因此他们可能从执行实际任务的真正开发人员那里收集了大量数据（在 openrouter 上他们被标记为这样）。现在，他们可以使用这些实时场景来进一步对模型进行后训练并进一步改进它们。

迫不及待地想看看将 k3 提炼到 dsv4 中是否会带来额外的改进。不管怎样，让廉价模型快速变得更好对社区来说是一件好事。特别是因为这些不会因提供商的一时兴起而“消失”。无论他们获得什么能力，都可以“永远”使用。而且，至少 Flash 可以在硬件 <10k 的情况下“在家”运行，这对于 glm/k3 较大的型号来说实际上是不可能/可行的。

The Internet in the early 2000s felt a little more special as compared to today, when 99.999 % of content is locked in a handful of walled gardens. I mean sure everything we had then is still possible but let’s be honest everything about the web is fine tuned to deliver ads to our eyeballs, browsers, operating systems and even protocols are being designed with ad delivery in mind. Just makes you wonder what stuff would thrive if ads didn’t exist. As of now every niche thing that gets successful will be invariably pulled into the ad ecosystem as it’s very hard to say no to money.

comments.author: inigyou
comments.textRawHtml:
LLMs are writing as well as humans for people who think writing words is the goal. Printing presses also write words better than humans. LLMs are solving the problem one layer higher than printing presses, but still several layers down from the top.

Note that LLMs aren't useless, since they have other strengths which can make them equal or better than humans in certain applications. For instance, they can tirelessly review code for silly mistakes, making them useful in cybersecurity.

children.author: docfort
children.textRawHtml: I think the first goal of writing is to talk to yourself. Without an external, unchanging scratchpad, most people cannot keep their thoughts truly straight. It can feel otherwise, but trying to write something about any tricky topic even a few pages in length can take a long time to be self-consistent. Clarifying it takes even longer, especially when you intend to share it. Writing as thinking is definitely a thing. I believe it’s the trickiest part of understanding how such interesting things pop out of a language model trained to predict the next token and rewarded with pleasing sequences. Since it is not thinking, it proves that certain sentences (most?) can be generated thoughtlessly.

children.author: WorldMaker
children.textRawHtml:
I think that LLM's are a broken mirror or maybe disco ball. What you get back is almost always a reflection of what you put in, just garbled through and with the reflections of so many other people. The best parts that I often get back are mostly just the stuff that I already put in it.

I think that's also where LLMs get the most dangerous. That ELIZA effect of telling you exactly what you told it but in a slightly rephrased way makes you think that you think that your ideas are genius. You've got someone "actively listening" and telling you whatever idea you just gave it was the best idea it ever heard.

That's not what you want from a serious writing partner. You want a writing partner to challenge you, to point out your mistakes and flaws, to make you better, to offer a truly different perspective to your own. You don't want a dark reflection from a "yes man" to spiral into.
children.textZhHtml:
我认为法学硕士是一面破碎的镜子或者迪斯科球。你得到的几乎总是你输入的内容的反映，只是乱码和许多其他人的反映。我经常得到的最好的部分大多只是我已经放入其中的东西。

我认为这也是法学硕士最危险的地方。 ELIZA 的效果是准确地告诉你你所说的内容，但以稍微改写的方式让你认为你认为你的想法是天才的。有人“积极倾听”并告诉你，无论你刚刚提出什么想法，它都是它听过的最好的想法。

这不是你想要从认真的写作伙伴那里得到的。你需要一个写作伙伴来挑战你，指出你的错误和缺陷，让你变得更好，为你提供真正不同的观点。你不想让“唯唯诺诺的人”陷入黑暗。

children.author: WorldMaker
children.textRawHtml:
I feel it is a net negative for me. One of my hobbies has always been fiction writing. The LLM reflections of my own writing become slot machines to me for cheap dopamine hits. It's not because LLMs are good at fiction writing, far from it, it's that LLMs are good at reflecting my own writing back to me in fun house mirror ways that amuse me and frustrate me and pleasantly surprise me.

That slot machine addiction gives me a lot of perspective on what LLMs are good at in coding versus what they appear to be good at. It's easy to characterize them as "over-eager junior developers" or "powerful rubber duck debuggers" but their biases are still your biases so long as you are the one writing the prompts. A lot of the "surprises" aren't intelligence but fun house mirror versions of the same biases you input into the system.

I keep referring to their coding capabilities as "legacy code as a service" and the addiction to the fictional equivalent only underscores that understanding of LLMs. You don't write the next great American novel getting a word salad of past great novels back full of the best and worst of your own writing. You don't write the next great American software getting a legacy code jumble of past great software back full of the best and worst of your own prompting.

At the end of the day I'm still a pragmatist and using the LLMs in my programming efforts, but I don't trust them as a partner, I use them as a tool. (A biased tool that I know needs a careful eye.)
children.textZhHtml:
我觉得这对我来说是一个净负面影响。我的爱好之一一直是小说写作。我自己写作的法学硕士反思对我来说成为了廉价多巴胺点击的老虎机。这并不是因为法学硕士擅长小说写作，远非如此，而是法学硕士擅长以游乐屋镜像的方式将我自己的写作反映给我，这些方式让我开心，让我沮丧，让我惊喜。

对老虎机的沉迷让我对法学硕士在编码方面的擅长与他们看起来擅长的方面有了很多看法。很容易将他们描述为“过于热切的初级开发人员”或“强大的橡皮鸭调试器”，但只要您是编写提示的人，他们的偏见仍然是您的偏见。很多“惊喜”并不是智力，而是你输入系统的相同偏见的游乐园镜像版本。

我一直将他们的编码能力称为“遗留代码即服务”，而对虚构的等价物的沉迷只会强调对法学硕士的理解。你写下一部伟大的美国小说时，不会把过去伟大小说的文字沙拉全部塞满你自己写作中最好和最差的部分。你编写下一个伟大的美国软件时，不会得到过去伟大软件的遗留代码混乱，其中充满了你自己提示的最好和最差的东西。

归根结底，我仍然是一个实用主义者，并在我的编程工作中使用法学硕士，但我不信任他们作为合作伙伴，我将他们用作工具。 （我知道这是一个有偏见的工具，需要仔细观察。）

Culture and art can teach something to its audience, unlike most of the garbage you likened it to. It's clear you don't hold it in much regard, since you compare it to outright scams (clickbait) and even imply that consuming fiction is basically done for virtue signalling.

But like it or not, humans are not computers. They are animals with messy, complex thinking and reasoning that is impossible to fully describe, and incredibly complex societal systems created from their chaotic interactions. These messy people don't learn from datasheets and reference manuals, even if you'd like it to be otherwise.

Of course, there's a place for non-fiction, I like some of it a lot. But art has subtlety to it - instead of smacking people in the face with data and lists of objective measurements, it can pry into them by using the human ability to imagine themselves in other shoes, experience emotions that aren't results of real life events, and much more. There is a reason why parents teach their children values by reading them fables or educational stories, not the legal code of their jurisdiction. And this is also why fiction actually changes the minds of people reading it, arguably doing it more effectively than nonfiction. Slop (clickbait, average tiktok content, whatever else you're imagining) doesn't make you feel new things or think of something you haven't thought of before, art does.

The aiens are also a bit of a copout. You're just assuming that there's bound to be this perfect species (that are effectively computers) that operate only on mathematics and discrete logic, who are obviously superior to us and can show us our wrong ways. What if computers aren't always superior? Or what if organic life requires some of that messiness you don't like to be viable? What if the aliens had their own weird things we could never relate to?
children.textZhHtml:
文化和艺术可以向观众传授一些东西，不像你所比喻的大多数垃圾。很明显，你不太重视它，因为你将其与彻头彻尾的骗局（点击诱饵）进行比较，甚至暗示消费小说基本上是为了传递美德信号。

但不管你喜欢与否，人类不是计算机。它们是具有无法完全描述的凌乱、复杂的思维和推理的动物，以及由它们混乱的相互作用创建的极其复杂的社会系统。这些混乱的人不会从数据表和参考手册中学习，即使您希望不是这样。

当然，非小说类作品也有一席之地，我非常喜欢其中的一些。但艺术也有它的微妙之处——它不是用数据和客观测量列表来打人们的脸，而是通过利用人类想象自己换位思考的能力来窥探它们，体验非现实生活事件结果的情感等等。父母通过阅读寓言或教育故事而不是其管辖范围内的法律来教导孩子价值观是有原因的。这也是为什么小说实际上改变了阅读它的人的思想，可以说比非小说更有效。 Slop（点击诱饵、普通的抖音内容，无论你想象的其他什么）不会让你感受到新事物或想到你以前没有想到过的东西，艺术却可​​以。

人工智能也有点逃避现实。你只是假设一定存在这种完美的物种（实际上是计算机），它们仅在数学和离散逻辑上运行，它们显然比我们优越，并且可以向我们展示错误的方法。如果计算机并不总是那么优越怎么办？或者，如果有机生命需要一些你不喜欢的混乱才能生存怎么办？如果外星人有他们自己的奇怪的东西我们永远无法联系怎么办？

children.author: underlipton
children.textRawHtml:
We already suspect that many non-human animals have a "sense of beauty" and a sense of humor. At least one other species spontaneously dances on the "beat" to music (parrots).

I think alien intelligence would be able to appreciate art and humor, even without necessarily feeling it viscerally, as we do. We know that our particular brands of them rely on highly-developed and specific aspects of our psychology, but at a basic level, they seem to fundamentally be about congruence, incongruence, expectation, and interpretation/perspective. Any embodied intelligence that can observe physical reality is capable of grokking those concepts.

我认为外星智慧生物能够欣赏艺术和幽默，即使不一定像我们一样发自内心地感受到它。我们知道，我们的特定品牌依赖于我们心理学的高度发展和特定方面，但在基本层面上，它们似乎从根本上是关于一致性、不一致、期望和解释/观点。任何能够观察物理现实的实体智能都能够理解这些概念。

I use YNAB (https://www.ynab.com/) for budgeting so I already had all of my financial data in a single source. Exporting the CSVs locally and asking Claude to be my financial advisor legitimately gave me good advice. Not just nagging me to save more (which is always useful), but how to organize my budget categories better, detecting longer term spending patterns I wasn't thinking much about, researching credit card reward programs based on my spending patterns, digging deep into interest and tax rates in way I never bothered etc.

That was the first time I felt like real people's jobs were threatened by AI. Financial advisors and tax accountants better adapt quickly.

children.author: thomaslord
children.textRawHtml:
This is the big pain-point for me with self-hosted budgeting software.

The corporate players in the space can jump through the security hoops and integrate with Plaid, but if I wanted to automatically pull my own data into the single-user budgeting tool I host entirely on my own network I need to pass the same security checks as a full-on fintech startup.

Currently I enter transactions manually, but manually reviewing multiple credit card and bank statements is a chore and I don't keep up with it as much as I should. To make things worse, since I ideally want a live view of my budget and not a post-statement-issuance monthly review, I'm constantly checking over transactions I've already entered when their ordering changes in my credit card company's app.

The closest thing to a potential solution involves extracting my Monarch Money session key from my browser and pulling data from their GraphQL endpoints with the help of an unofficial Python SDK. That doesn't solve the "relying on a subscription service" problem, but it would at least let me get my data into the custom budgeting tool I built that actually meets my needs.
children.textZhHtml:
这是我使用自托管预算软件的一大痛点。

该领域的企业参与者可以跳过安全圈并与 Plaid 集成，但如果我想自动将自己的数据提取到完全托管在自己网络上的单用户预算工具中，我需要通过与全面的金融科技初创公司相同的安全检查。

目前，我手动输入交易，但手动审查多张信用卡银行对账单是一件苦差事，我没有尽我所能地跟上它。更糟糕的是，由于我希望实时查看预算，而不是报表发行后的每月审核，因此当信用卡公司应用程序中的顺序发生变化时，我会不断检查已输入的交易。

最接近潜在解决方案的是从浏览器中提取我的 Monarch Money 会话密钥，并在非官方 Python SDK 的帮助下从其 GraphQL 端点提取数据。这并不能解决“依赖订阅服务”的问题，但它至少可以让我将数据输入到我构建的实际满足我需求的自定义预算工具中。
